t.6.95.1: Then there began between Rāma and Rāvaṇa a most cruel and mighty single combat of chariots, a battle that brought terror to all the worlds.
t.6.95.2: Then the army of the rākṣasas and the great host of the monkeys stood motionless, their weapons held ready in hand.
t.6.95.4: With their arms busy with various weapons, they stood still, their minds filled with amazement; and watching the battle, they did not strike one another.
t.6.95.3: Then, seeing the mighty man and the rākṣasa locked in combat, all the onlookers, their hearts bewildered, were struck with the utmost amazement.
t.6.95.5: As the rākṣasas gazed at Rāvaṇa and the vānaras at Rāghava with eyes wide in wonder, the army looked as still as a painted picture.
t.6.95.6: But those two, Rāghava and Rāvaṇa, having seen the omens there, with their minds resolved and their wrath unshaken, fought on as though without fear.
t.6.95.7: Kākutstha resolved, “I must conquer,” and Rāvaṇa, “I must die.” Then the two, firm in their resolve, displayed in battle the whole wealth of their own valor.
t.6.95.8: Then, out of anger, the mighty Daśagrīva fitted arrows to his bow and released them, aiming at the banner standing on Rāghava's chariot.
t.6.95.9: Those arrows, failing to reach that banner on Puraṃdara's chariot, only grazed its red staff and fell to the surface of the earth.
t.6.95.11: Aiming at Rāvaṇa's banner, he released a sharpened arrow, irresistible like a great serpent, blazing with its own splendor.
t.6.95.10: Rāma, valiant and fiercely enraged, drew back his bow and, braced for the fight, set his mind on repaying the deed in kind.
t.6.95.12: That arrow, having pierced the banner of Daśagrīva, went into the earth; and that chariot-banner of Rāvaṇa, cut down, fell upon the ground.
t.6.95.13: Seeing his banner torn down, the mighty Rāvaṇa, of exceedingly great strength, became as if ablaze in battle with a fire born of wrath.
t.6.95.14: Overcome by fury, Rāvaṇa, spewing forth a mighty shower of arrows, pierced the divine horses of Rāma with his shafts.
t.6.95.15: Though pierced by him, those monkeys did not falter, nor did they reel; they remained untroubled at heart, as if they had been struck with lotus stalks.
t.6.95.16: Then Rāvaṇa, seeing the composure of those horses, grew all the more furious and let loose a shower of arrows once again.
t.6.95.17: Maces and iron clubs, discuses and pestles, mountain peaks and trees, and likewise spears and battle-axes.
t.6.95.18: He, whose heart's resolve never flagged, let fall this rain of weapons fashioned by magic power; then he loosed arrows by the thousands.
t.6.95.19: In the battle there arose something mighty, made up of many weapons: tumultuous, terror-inspiring, dreadful, with dreadful echoes, and hard to withstand.
t.6.95.20: Turning away from Rāghava's chariot, Daśagrīva swiftly filled the sky all around over the monkey army with arrows, leaving no gap, and he loosed them with a heart free of all hesitation.
t.6.95.21: Seeing Rāvaṇa exerting himself in battle, wholly intent upon the fight, Kākutstha, as though laughing, fitted sharp arrows to his bow.
t.6.95.22: Then in the battle he released arrows by the hundreds of thousands; seeing them, Rāvaṇa made the sky gapless with his own arrows.
t.6.95.23: Then, by the brilliant shower of arrows discharged by those two, the shining sky appeared like a second sky, as if bound with arrows.
t.6.95.25: The two fought on without pause, shooting their arrows with left hand and right alike, and with their floods of arrows they made the sky seem as if it could no longer breathe.
t.6.95.24: As Rāma and Rāvaṇa loosed their arrows in that battle, no arrow went without its mark, none overshot its target, and none was fruitless.
t.6.95.26: Rāma struck down the horses of Rāvaṇa, and Rāvaṇa the horses of Rāma; thus the two then smote each other, each repaying in kind what the other had done.
